Subject: MAP & Redline Playbook: Procurement + Legal Introductions

Hi Sofia & Tom —

Thanks for taking the time to kick off this mutual action plan (MAP) conversation. Per our call yesterday, I wanted to put the high-level plan in writing and introduce the folks on our side who will help drive contracting, legal review, and procurement to close. Attached is a working MAP (MAP-v0.1.xlsx) and a first-pass SOW for your review.

Key ask: can you confirm who on your legal/procurement side will own redlines and who will be the final contract approver? If you can share names/emails, we’ll add them to the MAP and propose milestone owners.

Proposed milestones (high level):
- 10/05: Legal & procurement owners identified + initial redline window opens
- 10/12: Redline complete / final SOW agreed (target)
- 10/16: Exec approval and signature routing
- 10/20: Contract fully executed / go-live window confirmed

We know timelines can slip — if you have a preferred cadence for reviews (e.g., a single consolidated redline vs. iterative comments), call that out and we’ll adapt.

Next steps from our side: Lauren (cc’d) will own legal coordination and the redline tracker; Karthik will own commercial questions and the close timeline; Marissa will run the technical evaluation plan and onboarding checklist. I’ll own the MAP and be the primary point for overall cadence.

Attachments: MAP-v0.1.xlsx, SOW-draft-20261002.pdf

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP & Redline Playbook: Procurement + Legal Introductions

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear plan and for looping us in. I’ll be the legal owner for Medicor on the redline, and Tom (cc’d) is the procurement lead who will handle PO/timing. I attached our initial comments as a doc so you can see items we anticipate raising (primarily data residency, indemnity carve-outs, and an uptime SLA clarification).

We generally prefer a single consolidated redline (one round) for commercial terms and a short Q&A for technical items — keeps cycles shorter. That said, we can be flexible if Redwood prefers staged reviews.

We aim to finish internal review by 10/11 so that our redline lands with your team by 10/12. If anything blocks that, I’ll flag it early.

Best,
Sofia Moreno
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Medicor Health

Attachment: Legal-Comments-Medicor.docx

Sofia / Tom / Dylan —

Thanks for the intro. Quick note on process from Redwood legal so expectations are aligned:

1) Redline cadence: we prefer one consolidated redline exchange (your team sends comments; we return consolidated responses and proposed edits within 3 business days). If major commercial changes are requested, we’ll ask for a short follow-up call but will still aim to keep to the MAP timeline.

2) Primary concerns we’ll raise on our side: liability caps tied to quarterly ARR, data handling (we’ll propose standard DPA language), and an SLA appendix with remedy tiers. Please confirm whether Medicor requires any specific encryption/KMS commitments beyond what’s in the SOW.

3) Evidence & security items: Marissa will run a short eval on the integration work and will share a lightweight checklist (SOC 2 scope, expected data flows). For procurement: Tom, if you can confirm PO process and any internal funding codes, we’ll add an acceptance milestone tied to receipt of PO.

4) Timeline: If Medicor’s legal can turn comments by 10/11 we can return consolidated edits by 10/13 and route for internal approvals by 10/15. That keeps us on target for an execution window the week of 10/19.

5) Doc routing: we use DocuSign for final execution. I’ll attach a sample signature block to the tracker.

I’ll also maintain a redline tracker in the MAP workbook and populate it after we receive Medicor’s doc.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
